correctness.rationale: The factor equation has S'=U^TQU positive semidefinite, so the positive minimum eigenvalue of S cannot decrease; the Stiefel factor stays compact and S grows at most linearly. For B_r=I-P_r, the exact covariance defect is the initial positive semidefinite defect plus the integral of B_r Q B_r. Independently, in the range graph chart L=Y_BA(Y_AA)^(-1), L'(0)=Q_BA(Y_AA(0))^(-1). Differentiating Y'=Q-B_rQB_r gives D''_11=0, D''_13=-q12*q23/a, and D''_33=2*q23^2/b for D=Y2-Y1. The first derivative and initial form vanish on span(e1,e3). Substituting the stated z gives the coefficient -b*q12^2/(4*a^2) while the e2 form tends to b; smoothness gives both signs throughout a punctured time interval. The rank-one example yields -1/18. In dimension two the rank-two projector is the identity, so the established comparison with the full covariance rules out a counterexample there. A separate graph-chart integration gives z^TDz/t^2=-0.055661185 and -0.055567722 at t=0.01 and 0.001, respectively.

The open coupling condition and rank-one forcing isolate a concrete projector-rotation mechanism and rule out explaining the phenomenon as a time-stepping artifact.
